requirements.title: Level-2 expressions are the numeric-operator layer over level-1 expressions
requirements.definition: Level-2 expressions are built from level-1 expressions and optional numeric operators in four distinct precedence steps: exponentiation, multiplication/division, unary plus/minus at the first add-op position, and binary plus/minus in the left-recursive level-2 chain. The grammar specifies right recursion for power and left recursion for multiplication and binary addition/subtraction.
requirements.oracle:
Future precedence controls must use small integer literals with exact results and parenthesized companion controls where needed; they must not infer floating-point or overflow semantics.

Batch295 expressions 10.1.2.5-10.1.2.7 fixtures: one run/positive-control/f2023 program observes exact integer values for a level-1 base expression 2, right-recursive power 2**3**2=512, left-recursive multiplication/division 24/3*2=16, and add/subtract forms including 10-3-2=5 and -2**2=-4. Each assertion has a conforming feature mutation that changes the relevant operator, operand, or grouping and fails at run time.

requirements.title: A mult-operand is a level-1 expression optionally exponentiated by a mult-operand
requirements.definition: The mult-operand syntax is a level-1-expr followed optionally by power-op and another mult-operand, making unparenthesized exponentiation right-recursive within the grammar.
requirements.oracle:
Power negatives must use the valid '**' token and valid left operand; malformed operator spellings belong to R1008 or lexical rules.

requirements.title: An add-operand is a left-recursive chain of mult-operands joined by mult-op
requirements.definition: The add-operand syntax is either a mult-operand or an add-operand followed by mult-op and a mult-operand, giving multiplication and division the same level and left-recursive grouping.
requirements.oracle:
Plans must keep operands numeric and defined so future diagnostics are syntactic for missing operands, not semantic type errors from 10.1.5.

requirements.title: A level-2 expression is an add-operand with optional unary or binary add-op
requirements.definition: The level-2-expr syntax is an add-operand, optionally preceded by an add-op, or a left-recursive level-2-expr followed by add-op and add-operand. This admits unary plus/minus and binary plus/minus at the level-2 layer.
requirements.oracle:
Unary and binary add-op plans must distinguish position. Missing-operand negatives must not also introduce malformed operator tokens or undeclared names.

requirements.title: The power operator token is double asterisk
requirements.definition: The power-op token is '**'. It is the token used by R1005; this rule does not define operand types or exponentiation interpretation.
requirements.oracle:
Do not attribute all uses of '*' to R1008; '*' is valid R1009. Any negative must place the token where only power-op is syntactically possible.

requirements.title: Multiplication operators are asterisk and slash
requirements.definition: The mult-op alternatives are '*' and '/'. This rule defines the tokens for R1006, not numeric type admissibility or division semantics.

requirements.definition: The add-op alternatives are '+' and '-'. The tokens can appear in unary or binary positions through R1007; interpretation and operand validity are elsewhere.
